extracted.intended_audience: Applicants to NIH research grants, institutional training and career development awards, and individual fellowships (people preparing NIH grant applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how to address rigor, transparency, and reproducibility in NIH grant, career development, training, and fellowship applications and what reviewers will evaluate. Covers expectations for assessing prior research, experimental design, biological variables, resource authentication, and training requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor of the prior research
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are expected to describe the general strengths and weaknesses in the rigor of the prior research (both published and unpublished) that serves as the key support for the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the term 'scientific premise' in application instructions and review language. The consideration should include attention to the rigor of previous experimental designs and the incorporation of relevant biological variables and authentication of key resources. Applicants are expected to include plans to address any weaknesses or gaps identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific rigor (experimental design, methods, analysis, interpretation, reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific rigor is the strict application of the scientific method to ensure robust and unbiased experimental design, methodology, analysis, interpretation and reporting of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH expects full transparency in proposing and reporting experimental details so that reviewers may assess the proposed research and others may reproduce and extend the findings. Applicants should propose rigorous, unbiased methods and analyses and describe how they will ensure robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of relevant biological variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Biological variables, such as sex, age, weight, and underlying health conditions, are often critical factors affecting health or disease and must be considered in research designs, analyses, and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, sex is frequently ignored in animal study designs and analyses; NIH expects sex as a biological variable will be factored into research designs, analyses, and reporting in vertebrate animal and human studies. Strong justification from literature, preliminary data, or other considerations must be provided for applications proposing to study only one sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Key biological and/or chemical resources (including, but not limited to, cell lines, specialty chemicals, antibodies and other biologics) must be authenticated when they are integral to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources may differ across laboratories or over time and may have qualities that influence data. The quality of resources is critical to reproducibility. Each investigator must determine which resources used in their research fit the criteria of 'key resources' and therefore require authentication. Guidance, FAQs, and a required 'Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources' attachment (when applicable) are referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans to address weaknesses or gaps in prior research
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must include plans to address any weaknesses or gaps identified in the rigor of the prior research that supports the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such plans should be described within the Research Strategy section. For research grants and career development awards, applicants are instructed to describe plans to address weaknesses in prior research; reviewers will evaluate whether those plans adequately mitigate limitations in the prior evidence base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and reporting of experimental details
rubrics_metrics.description: Full transparency in proposing and reporting experimental details is required so that reviewers can assess the proposed research and others can reproduce and extend the findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide sufficient methodological and reporting detail (e.g., experimental design, analytic approach, resource identification/authentication) in the application Research Strategy and relevant attachments to allow assessment and reproducibility. This expectation is part of NIH's definition of scientific rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in rigorous experimental design and reproducibility (program-level requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional training and institutional career development applications must include a description of how the program and faculty will provide training in rigorous research design and relevant data science and quantitative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH planned requirement (for applications with due dates on or after May 25, 2020) expands the requirement to include a 'Plan for Instruction in Methods for Enhancing Reproducibility' attachment for all applicants where applicable. This also applies to institutional career development, individual career development, and individual fellowship applications (where training goals/objectives should address acquiring skills in rigorous design, methods, quantitative approaches, and data analysis/interpretation). See NOT-OD-20-033 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship Research Strategy required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual fellowship Research Strategy attachments must address specific elements relating to rigor and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship candidates will be expected to describe (a) the strengths and weaknesses in the rigor of the prior research that serves as key support for the proposed project, (b) plans to address any weaknesses in the rigor of the prior research, (c) how the experimental objectives proposed will achieve robust and unbiased results, and (d) how relevant biological variables are factored into research designs and analyses. If applicable, fellowship candidates must include the Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources attachment.
